support-ian: Hey team — we're seeing a customer repro where the Go SDK returns `context deadline exceeded` and the backend never logs the request. Happens intermittently when the app sets a short context deadline but http.Client.Timeout is larger. Repro below, can someone sanity-check?

support-ian: Repro snippet:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 250*time.Millisecond)
defer cancel()
cli := &http.Client{Timeout: 5*time.Second, Transport: &http.Transport{ /* default */ }}
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, bytes.NewReader(body))
resp, err := cli.Do(req)
if err != nil {
    log.Printf("do err: %v", err) // -> context deadline exceeded
}
// server side: no incoming conn recorded for these requests
```

support-ian: Our SDK wraps http.Client and retries on transient errors. Logs show the SDK deciding to retry after `context deadline exceeded` and then the call vanishes (no server logs) — suspect the retry path is not checking ctx.Done() or the transport is racing with cancel.

ben-eng: Can you paste the SDK version and go version? Also the transport config (IdleConnTimeout, KeepAlive) and whether you're using a custom DialContext or proxy?

support-ian: go1.20.7, redwood-go-sdk v0.9.3. No proxy. Transport is mostly default; we didn't change IdleConnTimeout. No custom DialContext.

ben-eng: Ok. Two quick thoughts: (1) if http.Client.Timeout > ctx deadline, the net.Conn may still be used by the client after ctx cancels and some race can drop the request before it reaches server. (2) our retry wrapper should bail if ctx is done. Does the SDK log the retry reason?

support-ian: SDK logs: `retry attempt=1 reason="ctx deadline exceeded"` then it calls Do again but with the same `req` (which has the original ctx attached). The second Do sometimes returns immediate `context canceled` or the SDK aborts. Server still doesn't see a TCP handshake in some repros.

tanya: This pattern is a classic context-vs-client-timeout mismatch. If you rely on per-request ctx cancellation, prefer http.Client.Timeout = 0 (no global timeout) and let the ctx drive cancellation. Otherwise the client can leave sockets half-closed. Two quick workarounds: set `Transport.DisableKeepAlives=true` for the client used in tests, or set `Client.Timeout` slightly above ctx deadline and ensure retries check `ctx.Err()` before attempting a new Do.

samir: Also check the RoundTripper wrapper in the SDK — if it clones `req` incorrectly or reuses the same body (non-rewindable) across retries, the second Do could return before even sending. If the body is an io.ReadCloser backed by a stream that EOFs on first read, subsequent retries won't send anything.

samir: Quick check list:
- confirm request body is `io.NopCloser(bytes.NewReader(body))` (rewindable)
- make sure retries call `req = req.Clone(ctx)` or recreate request so the context is current
- log at transport/dial level (tcpdump?) to see if SYN leaves the client

support-ian: Good call — the repro used bytes.NewReader so rewindable, but our SDK had a helper that wrapped the body in a counting reader that closed on first attempt. I'll try with a fresh request creation per retry.

ben-eng: If you can capture pcap showing no SYN when ctx deadline occurs that proves the cancel happened before connect. Also post the minimal failing test and I'll run it locally.

support-ian: Will do. One more oddity — when running in k8s with our liveness probe the issue spikes. Could be connection pooling interactions under load.

tanya: For k8s load, I'd lean DisableKeepAlives=false (keepalive helps) but ensure IdleConnTimeout is nonzero and not too short. For quick mitigation: make SDK check `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() default: }` before attempting a retry.

devops-bot: [automated] Uploaded logs: /var/log/support/2374209921/pcap.tar.gz

support-ian: Uploaded a small test that reproduces locally in ~30s; includes pcap and go test. Posting link in the thread soon. Thanks for the pointers — will update when I have a deterministic repro. :pray:

ben-eng: Great, ping me when posted and I'll triage. If it's a bug in our retry wrapper we'll cut a patch (ensure retries are ctx-aware and recreate request bodies). :+1:

support-ian: Update (later): confirmed root cause: SDK retry wrapper reused a non-rewindable body and retried after ctx timed out; sometimes the retry path raced with cancel and the transport dropped the connection. Fix submitted: recreate request per retry + check ctx.Err() before Do. Tests added.

support-ian: Closing the support ticket after patch rollout — customer confirmed no more silent drops.
